name: plane_rigid_short_slide_5n
parameter_origin: Illustrative synthetic values; not measured properties of a named commercial material.
material_label: Rigid reference at 5 N, 1 mm slide
model_notes: Load-controlled at 5 N; travel is an outcome.

The slide is two phases. From t = 3.00 to 3.09 every one of the 1080 contact points sticks, chattering stays at 0 and each substep converges in two iterations at the full increment. The trouble starts the instant the first points slip, at a global traction ratio of 0.10 against mu_s = 0.6: they are the perimeter points, where the gel's free edge drives pressure to zero and mu*p with it.

By t = 3.13 the same ring reports an abrupt contact -> no-contact change, immediately followed by a distorted SOLID185 trial iterate. A point that opens releases its stored elastic energy at once, and quasi-statically the rest of the interface must absorb it inside the same equilibrium.
Mass is what makes that release well posed, so the slide is integrated with inertia. It is also what stick-slip is: a dynamic limit cycle has no quasi-static equivalent.
Gel elements stay healthy at every converged state - worst corner Jacobian ratio 0.91, none below 0.5 - so the distortion lives in rejected iterates and refining the gel mesh would not address it.
